title: How I Make a Cosy Kawaii Sticker Sheet (Fixture Video)
author: Cosy Studio (fixture)

segments.text: Hi friends, and welcome back to the cosy studio!
Today we're making a kawaii sticker sheet from start to finish.
I'll show you my canvas setup, my favourite brushes, and how I export for printing.
Grab a warm drink and let's get started.
First, open a new canvas at twelve by twelve inches, three hundred DPI.
That gives us plenty of room for about twenty stickers.
Now pick a soft pastel palette. I'm using my cosy winter colours today.
Sketch loose shapes first. Don't worry about clean lines yet.
Little mugs, mittens, snowflakes and a sleepy cat are perfect for this theme.
Once you like the layout, lower the sketch opacity and add a new layer for line art.
Use a monoline brush so every sticker has the same line weight.
Keep at least an eighth of an inch between stickers so the cutter has space.
Next, flat colours. Fill each shape on its own layer under the line art.
Add tiny blush marks and highlights, that's what makes them feel kawaii.
Now the white border. Duplicate everything, merge, and add an outline.
This border is what the cutting machine follows, so keep it smooth.
Export a PNG with a transparent background for print and cut.
And export a flat JPG preview for your listing photos.
Before you list it, do a test print on plain paper to check the colours.
If the colours look dull, bump the saturation a little and print again.
That's it! You now have a sticker sheet ready for your shop.
In the next video I'll show you how I write titles and tags for Etsy.
Thanks for watching, and see you in the cosy studio next time.
